name: tdot
description: An open-source browser GIS for Toronto — police-reported crime by neighbourhood, the full open housing record (rental buildings, community and subsidized housing, health and fire violations, the development pipeline, census dwelling values), TTC networks, cycling, green spaces and boundaries, as toggleable MapLibre layers. Finds the city-owned lots affordable housing could actually be built on — vacant land, surface parking and surplus property, scored on size, transit and surplus status, each full lot boundary highlighted on the map — and has a 3-D mode that tilts the camera, extrudes real building heights and raises each candidate lot to the massing it could carry. Includes a model that predicts a building's RentSafeTO inspection score from open data and maps which buildings score worse than their peers, ten themes that repaint the map itself and not just the console, and an MCP server (stdio + streamable HTTP) publishing all 18 map tools so any MCP client can drive the live map. Every source is public, key-free open data.
